Crosswalks: mapping model columns to collections

Source: R/crosswalk.R
crosswalk.Rd

A crosswalk is a data frame that tells conjoint_df() how the model-format columns of a utilities data frame map to user-facing level names and to the collections (conjoint attributes) they belong to.

Details

Each row of a crosswalk describes one level column:

  • old_name: the model-format column name, A[NUM]B[NUM], as it appears in the utilities data.

  • user_name: the name the column takes after conjoint_df() renames it. Must be unique across the crosswalk.

  • collection_name: the attribute the level belongs to, e.g. "Brand".

  • collection_order: an integer rank giving the level's position in an ordered collection, or NA for an unordered collection. A collection must be either fully ranked or fully NA; partial ranks are an error.

  • absence (optional): a logical flag marking the level that means the attribute is absent (see collection). At most one level per collection may be flagged. If the column is missing, no level is treated as absence.

All of old_name, user_name, and collection_name must be character. Every old_name must be a column of the utilities data, and each old_name may appear only once. Columns of the utilities data that are not listed in the crosswalk (e.g. IDs or demographics) are left unchanged.

The crosswalk is coerced to a tibble, so $ and [[ do not partially match column names.

See also

conjoint_df() builds a conjoint data frame from a crosswalk, collection and ordered_collection() describe the collections it creates, and example_crosswalk is a worked example.

Examples

head(example_crosswalk)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   old_name user_name collection_name collection_order
#>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>                      <dbl>
#> 1 A1B1     Northwind Brand                         NA
#> 2 A1B2     Cascade   Brand                         NA
#> 3 A1B3     Meridian  Brand                         NA
#> 4 A2B1     $199      Price                          1
#> 5 A2B2     $299      Price                          2
#> 6 A2B3     $399      Price                          3

conjoint_df(example_utilities, example_crosswalk)
#> <conjoint_df>: 5 collections
#>   • Brand
#>   • Price (ordered)
#>   • Battery (ordered)
#>   • Storage (ordered)
